revision_summary: Overall the analysis is well-grounded on quotes (no critical fabrications found) and the outcome dispute is correctly supported. Targeted fixes needed on rerun: (1) Populate the empty multi_touch_patterns array — the 00:04-00:13 exchange ('Is this Daniel again?... This is Ella Lagany on Fuller') is direct evidence of a continuation call and belongs in this dedicated field rather than scattered as speculation across starting_state and cherry_pick_moments. (2) Reconsider the 'reactive' rep_intent classification — given the schema's explicit call_shape allowance for context-justified beat compression on calls where qualification was captured elsewhere, this call's structure (skip straight to scheduling) is better read as appropriate handling of a known repeat lead, not a reactive/gap-driven pattern. (3) Fix the schema reference mismatch in cherry_pick_moments[1]: the classification label 'conditional_booking' doesn't match what's actually being flagged (an incomplete button_up sequence missing the fair-handshake and no-driving/computer lines) — relabel as button_up_incomplete or similar, keep the button_up.is_that_fair_handshake citation. (4) Soften cherry_pick_moments[2] setter_scope_creep — the schema's own scope_creep_signals examples (panel tech, pricing, technical debates) are more severe than listing generic appointment-agenda categories (estimate/design/warranty/incentives); this is closer to legitimate button-up expectation-setting and should be reclassified or downgraded. (5) Add positive credit for well-executed moments: the 01:11-01:53 scheduling exchange (firm time anchor executed cleanly against a weekend/morning-only constraint) and the customer's proactive appointment-process question at 02:23 are engagement/procedural-success signals that should balance the otherwise gap-focused cherry_pick_moments list.
